extracted.intended_audience: news reporters and journalism students covering exhibitions, entertainments, and special occasions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reporting and writing news stories about exhibitions, shows, fairs, parades, banquets, holiday celebrations, and similar special occasions, emphasizing selection, tone, and descriptive technique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of story classification
rubrics_metrics.description: News stories in this division may be grouped in two classes: (1) those of display, such as exhibitions, shows, fairs, and parades, and (2) those of banquets, holiday celebrations, and other special occasions, such as college commencements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the subject matter covers a wide range, the method of handling the news is much the same. Use the classification to decide emphasis and treatment appropriate to display events versus ceremonial/social occasions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose — portray events attractively and bring out spirit
rubrics_metrics.description: The aim in these stories is not only to portray attractively the events and scenes but to bring out the spirit of the occasion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is generally a dominant note in all these events, and the effectiveness of the description can be greatly heightened by selecting those details that bring out this note. Selection and presentation of details should be made from the point of view of their value as showing the mood of the occasion rather than merely recording incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy as truth of sentiment
rubrics_metrics.description: Accuracy in news stories of this kind is not simply faithfulness to fact, but truth of sentiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Untruthfulness lies in adding fictitious details in an effort to heighten the appeal, and in substituting sentimentality for true sentiment. Do not invent or exaggerate emotional elements; aim for truthful depiction of the event's feeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of picturesque and significant phases
rubrics_metrics.description: The chief problem in writing these stories is to select picturesque and significant phases from the large mass of available material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the available material, pick those scenes and incidents that are both vivid and significant; avoid attempting a complete catalogue of everything that happened. Focus on elements that will convey the event's dominant impression to readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dynamic descriptive treatment — one impression over completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: The description is of the so-called dynamic type, in that all of the details are selected with the purpose of bringing out one impression rather than of giving a complete picture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These events offer one of the few chances in news writing for pure description. Use vivid, selective details to produce a strong single impression; resist the temptation to cram in every factual element and thereby dilute the effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use emotional appeal appropriate to specific holidays and occasions
rubrics_metrics.description: In descriptions of holiday celebrations an emotional appeal is possible because every festival and holiday has its own particular sentiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match the emotional tone to the occasion: Christmas — generosity and children's day; Memorial Day — patriotic reverence; Fourth of July — patriotic jollification; Thanksgiving — feasting. For banquets and occasions where good fellowship is dominant, use a lighter descriptive vein.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of speeches and toasts within event stories
rubrics_metrics.description: When speeches and toasts are delivered in connection with these events, they are treated like other speeches and are fitted into the story as incidents of the occasion, or, if they are of sufficient significance, they may be played up as the feature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide whether a speech is an incidental detail (embed briefly as part of scene) or the story's feature (give fuller coverage and prominence) based on its significance to the event or audience.
